title: Cap. II Sol. Arg. 5 close: Augustine / Gregory / Aquinas — all = kinds, not foresight-cooperation
pass_a_gloss: Finally, if anyone stubbornly contends that the Apostle's words are to be understood of God's efficacious will, he will never extricate himself if he takes the place otherwise than it was formerly explained by Augustine, Gregory, and the Scholastics. So Augustine in De correptione et gratia chapter 14: God wills all men to be saved, that all the predestined be understood, because every kind of men is in them. And Gregory: He wills all men to be saved, because from every kind of men he elects those whom he draws to the joy of eternal salvation. On 1 Kings book 5 chapter 4. Aquinas finally in the Commentaries on these very words: It is a distribution for the kinds of individuals, not for the individuals of the kinds. Since therefore this place does not prove that God by the will of good pleasure wills the salvation of all and each, much less does it prove that God elects men to salvation from foresight of future cooperation by which they accommodate themselves to this will of God.
pass_b_english: Last: if someone still insists Paul's words mean God's efficacious will, he will never get free unless he reads the place as Augustine, Gregory, and the scholastics long did. Augustine, On Rebuke and Grace 14: "God wills all men to be saved" — understand all the predestined, because every kind of human being is among them. Gregory: he wills all men to be saved because from every kind of people he elects those he draws to the joy of eternal salvation (on 1 Kings, book 5, ch. 4). Aquinas on the same words: the distribution is for the kinds of individuals, not for the individuals of the kinds. So this text does not prove that by the will of good pleasure God wills the salvation of every single person — and far less that he elects people to salvation from foresight of the future cooperation by which they would fit themselves to that will.
source_text: Postremo, si quis obstinate contendat verba Apostoli de efficaci voluntate Dei esse intelligenda, is nunquam se expediet, si aliter locum capiat quam ab Augustino, Gregorio & Scholasticis olim fuit explicatus. Sic Augustinus de corrept. & grat. cap. 14. Deus vult omnes homines salvos fieri, ut intelligantur omnes praedestinati, quia omne genus hominum est in iis. Et Gregorius, Omnes homines vult salvos fieri, quia ex omni hominum genere eligit, quos ad gaudium aeternae salutis trahit. In 1. Reg. lib. 5. cap. 4. Aquinas denique in Commentariis ad haec ipsa verba, Est distributio pro generibus singulorum, non pro singulis generum. Quandoquidem ergo hic locus non probat Deum voluntate beneplaciti velle salutem omnium & singulorum, multo minus probat Deum eligere homines ad salutem ex praescientia futurae cooperationis, qua se accommodent huic voluntati Dei.
